{"candidate_rtl":"module alu_64bit(
    input [63:0] a, b,
    input [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [63:0] sum
);
    wire arithmetic;
    wire subtract;
    wire reverse_subtract;
    wire [63:0] adder_a;
    wire [63:0] adder_b;
    wire [64:0] arithmetic_ext;
    reg [63:0] logic_result;

    assign arithmetic = ~Oper[2] & ~(Oper[1] & Oper[0]);
    assign subtract = Oper[1] | Oper[0];
    assign reverse_subtract = Oper[1] & ~Oper[0];
    assign adder_a = reverse_subtract ? b : a;
    assign adder_b = subtract ? (reverse_subtract ? ~a : ~b) : b;
    assign arithmetic_ext = {1'b0, adder_a} + {1'b0, adder_b} + {{64{1'b0}}, subtract};

    always @(*) begin
        case (Oper)
            3'b011: logic_result = a | b;
            3'b100: logic_result = a & b;
            3'b101: logic_result = a ^ b;
            3'b110: logic_result = a ~^ b;
            default: logic_result = 64'b0;
        endcase
    end

    always @(*) begin
        if (arithmetic)
            sum = arithmetic_ext[63:0];
        else
            sum = logic_result;
    end
endmodule","bottleneck":"The critical path is the 64-bit add/subtract carry chain, followed by operand-selection and final operation-selection multiplexing.","rewrite":"Share one 65-bit adder for addition, both subtraction directions, and the ignored carry result. Decode arithmetic operations separately from the four bitwise operations so the arithmetic datapath is selected only once at the output.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected modest improvement in maximum data arrival from eliminating separate add/subtract datapaths and exposing a single carry-chain implementation; the exact gain depends on whether baseline synthesis already performs equivalent arithmetic sharing.","area_or_other_cost":"Likely lower or similar mapped area due to the shared adder, with small decode and mux logic. The implementation remains well below the stated area cap and introduces no storage or extra ports.","functional_boundaries":"For Oper=000, sum is the low 64 bits of a+b; 001 is a-b; 010 is b-a; 011 is a|b; 100 is a&b; 101 is a^b; 110 is a~^b; and 111 produces 64'b0. All arithmetic carries are truncated exactly as in the original output assignment, and all input bit patterns are supported."}
